## 4. Predicted Symptoms: CPU Throttling vs Memory Pressure
| Diagnostic Symptom | CPU Quota Throttling | Memory Pressure / OOM |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Primary Telemetry** | CPU PSI (`cpu:some`) elevated; high run queue | Memory PSI (`memory:some`, `memory:full`) elevated |
| **Process State** | Runnable tasks may be delayed; verify cpu.stat quota-throttling deltas | Tasks blocked in uninterruptible sleep (D) reclaiming RAM |
| **Context Switching** | Elevated involuntary context switches (`ru_nivcsw`) | Reclaim, faults and I/O may increase; none is a unique pressure signature |
| **Crash Signature** | Does not terminate process; causes latency spikes | 137 is consistent with SIGKILL; match OOM logs/counters before attribution |
| **Kernel Log Proof** | CPU CFS bandwidth throttling counters increment | `Memory cgroup out of memory: Killed process` in dmesg |
| **Corrective Action** | Review CPU demand, quota and scheduling capacity | Review memory demand, limits and leaks before choosing a change |

## 5. Verification Conclusion
The evidence establishes that MemAvailable accounts for reclaimable page cache and confirms that container cgroup memory.max limits operate independently of host VM physical memory capacity.

=== Standard Operating Procedure: Boundary-Ordered Diagnostics ===
Stage 1: [DNS Resolution]
  Command:   dig +short api.example.com
  Validates: Shows the selected resolver answer; reachability is separate
Stage 2: [TCP Socket Establishment]
  Command:   ss -tna | grep <IP>:<PORT>
  Validates: A matching ESTAB record supports a local established socket, not application health
Stage 3: [Packet Interface Path]
  Command:   tcpdump -nn -c 5 host <IP>
  Validates: Packets visible at the selected capture point; absence does not locate a firewall drop
Stage 4: [Application Transport / TLS]
  Command:   curl -Iv https://api.example.com
  Validates: TLS certificate verified and HTTP status received
Stage 5: [Structured Payload Schema]
  Command:   python3 / jq select(.status >= 500)
  Validates: Payload contains valid JSON and parses status codes
-----------------------------------------------------------------
Diagnostic Principle: Test one boundary at a time; never jump to application conclusions before transport proof.
# Command-Line Diagnostic Toolchain Audit Report

## 1. Summary
- **Timestamp:** 2026-10-17T03:01:39Z
- **Investigator:** Site Reliability Engineering
- **Target Fixture:** `orders.jsonl` (5 structured records)

## 2. Text Search vs Structured Parsing Comparison
| Tool / Methodology | Query Syntax | Result Observed | Accuracy Assessment |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Naive Grep** | `grep -i "error"` | 0 records returned (exit 1) | **FALSE NEGATIVE**: Missed all 5xx outages |
| **Positional Regex** | `grep "503"` | 1 record returned | **FRAGILE**: Matches non-status numbers |
| **Structured JSON** | `select(.status >= 500)` | 2 records returned (`ord-102`, `ord-105`) | **FIXTURE RESULT**: Two supplied 5xx records selected; not production accuracy |

## 3. Network Boundary Tool Selection
- **DNS Boundary:** Use `dig` to verify resolver answers independently of transport.
- **Kernel Socket Boundary:** Use `ss -tln` to verify local port binding and backlog queue depth.
- **Packet Interface Boundary:** Use `tcpdump` with BPF filters to verify visibility at the selected capture point.
- **Application Boundary:** Use `curl -v` to isolate TLS negotiation from HTTP status handling.

## 4. Conclusion
Unstructured text searching must never be used as an acceptance gate for structured JSON telemetry. Diagnostic procedures must test boundaries hierarchically from DNS through socket, packet, transport, and schema validation.
